$comment: Coverage thresholds and the layer-to-suite binding (DOD-008; EP-007 M1). TESTING.md carries this same JSON verbatim in its 'Coverage targets (DOD-008)' section, and the two must stay byte-identical in content: the gate reads THIS file, and the test suite asserts the two agree. Lowering a target requires a specification change with a recorded rationale; lowering one to obtain a pass is prohibited (DOD-027).
$layerBinding: WHICH SUITES MEASURE WHICH LAYER, AND WHY IT IS WRITTEN DOWN. src/ has five directories (adapters, application, domain, http, infrastructure) while the target table names seven layers, and the blueprint's own layer-to-suite table names test ROOTS THIS REPOSITORY DOES NOT USE (tests/application/, tests/adapters/, tests/api/, tests/e2e/, tests/infrastructure/, tests/release/). The binding below is therefore the mapping that actually exists, derived from what each suite imports, and every entry states its basis.

layers.name: domain
layers.basis: the domain is imported by every pure suite; measured 2026-09-16 at 95.19/92.12/95.20 against 90/85/95

layers.name: application
layers.basis: the contract suites drive the application layer through its ports, which is where its rules are asserted

layers.name: adapters
layers.basis: the real adapters are exercised against PostgreSQL in tests/db and tests/integration; src/adapters/agent is EXCLUDED here because the target table names it as its own layer (mcp) and counting one file in two layers would make both numbers describe the same code

layers.name: http
layers.basis: route and envelope behaviour is asserted in the contract suites; the black-box suite drives the real server over HTTP

layers.name: mcp
layers.basis: there is no src/mcp directory: the MCP tool surface IS src/adapters/agent (the tool registry and the effect budget), and tests/contract/mcp-least-privilege.test.ts is what asserts it

layers.name: infrastructure
layers.basis: the psql runner, the migration runner and the composition root are exercised where they are used: against a real database

layers.name: ui
layers.note: WHAT THIS NUMBER DOES NOT SEE, STATED BY THE GATE ITSELF: the browser stage (tests/ui/**.spec.ts, Playwright) drives all 25 declared routes and is where this layer's required test kind lives, and Node's built-in coverage cannot instrument it. The figure below is therefore the Node-renderable half only. It is reported as a floor, never as the layer's whole proof.
layers.basis: EACH MODULE IS MEASURED ONCE, IN THE IDENTITY THE CONTRACT SUITES ACTUALLY EXERCISE, AND THE EXCLUSIONS ARE PART OF THAT. The UI is TSX, so Node's test runner cannot load a component; tests/contract/render-support.ts mirrors ui/src/** into .cache-ui-render/** as .js and the suites import the mirror. The plain-TypeScript modules (api/**, lib/**, copy/**, routes/*.ts) are different: the suites import THEM from ui/src directly. Both identities are named above, and the mirror's copies of those plain-TS modules are EXCLUDED, because a component's import of `.cache-ui-render/<pid>/api/client.js` is a DIFFERENT module instance from the `ui/src/api/client.ts` the test drives — the mirror copy is loaded but never called, so counting it would be counting one module twice, once as itself and once as a dead copy. MEASURED: with the dead copies counted the layer reads 80.46/85.80/66.96, and with each module measured once it reads 89.49/86.19/87.57. Nothing is excluded that any test could cover: every excluded path is a duplicate of a path that is measured.
